genZNote: Get infected with a second, different serotype and your risk of severe disease actually goes up — your own antibodies end up helping the virus.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human bloodstream and tissues during infection; Aedes mosquito midgut/salivary glands during the extrinsic incubation period
habitat.hostAssociation: Human-mosquito transmission cycle; four distinct serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4)
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans; Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes

identificationClues: Diagnosed by NS1 antigen testing (early illness) or IgM/IgG serology; PCR confirms and serotypes the virus
Severe disease risk (dengue hemorrhagic fever/shock syndrome) is markedly increased on secondary infection with a different serotype (antibody-dependent enhancement)
Classic "breakbone fever" — high fever with severe myalgia/arthralgia and retro-orbital headache
Petechial or maculopapular rash may develop

diseases: Severe dengue (dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus mosquito
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common arboviral infections globally, especially in tropical and subtropical regions; incidence has expanded substantially in recent decades with mosquito vector range expansion
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: NS1 antigen is most useful in the first few days of illness, while IgM/IgG serology becomes more useful later in the clinical course

examFacts.importantDisease: Dengue fever; severe dengue (hemorrhagic fever/shock syndrome)
examFacts.importantTest: NS1 antigen test; IgM/IgG serology; RT-PCR
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Secondary infection with a different dengue serotype substantially raises the risk of severe disease via antibody-dependent enhancement
